role: Indian independence leader and advocate of satyagraha (1869–1948)
summary: Gandhi advocated nonviolent self-rule, decentralised village life and economic equality through voluntary social transformation. His later writings defended religious freedom and equal citizenship while grounding political action in spiritual and moral commitments.

universal-healthcare.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Karachi resolution he moved called for a living wage for industrial workers, and he wanted wages set at a level giving decent food, housing and clothing (Bombay Chronicle 28 October 1944); he did not endorse a legal minimum-wage rise as such.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred: called an economics that lets the strong amass wealth at the expense of the weak a false science (Harijan 9 October 1937) and criticised the mill-owners' reliance on supply and demand in the Autobiography (An Instructive Dialogue).

public-ownership.rationale: Said he would have state ownership where large numbers must work together (Harijan 1 September 1946), and the Constructive Programme says heavy industries will be centralized and nationalized; the Karachi resolution asked for state control of key industries. He wanted these to be a small part of a mostly village economy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Argued in Harijan (31 July 1937, in 'Death Duties', India of My Dreams ch. 64) that holding inordinate wealth is a crime against Indian humanity and that taxation of riches had no upper limit, citing 70 percent rates elsewhere; the Karachi resolution he moved in 1931 also called for progressive income tax and a graduated inheritance tax.

unions-good.rationale: He praises organised nonviolent labour and its ability to secure workers’ rights.

property-fundamental.rationale: Held that a wealthy person's wealth beyond an honourable livelihood belongs to the community (trusteeship, Harijan 3 June 1939) and said the state may deprive owners of property with minimum violence if they do not act as trustees (Modern Review 1933, India of My Dreams ch. 16).

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposed great trusts and concentration of industry (Young India 24 July 1924) and the Karachi programme asked for state control of key industries and control of usury; no general plan for regulating corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Wrote that labourers should rise to the status of proprietors (Young India 16 February 1921) and that in state-owned large industries the product of labour should vest in the workers through the state (Harijan 1 September 1946); he did not draw a detailed scheme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Advocated total legal prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs (Karachi resolution 1931; Constructive Programme, 'Prohibition'), saying he would close every liquor shop without compensation if made dictator for an hour (Young India 25 June 1931).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred: described a leader as only first among equals who must follow the people's ethics (Young India 8 December 1921) and feared concentrated state power (Modern Review 1935, India of My Dreams ch. 20).

state-harmful.rationale: Called the state organized violence and a soulless machine, said the ideal non-violent state is an ordered anarchy where the state is best that governs least (Young India 2 July 1931; Harijan 16 September 1946), but accepted that some state and police remain necessary for now.

limit-guns.rationale: Contested: the Karachi resolution he moved guaranteed the right to keep and bear arms subject to regulation, and he called disarming India the blackest act of British rule (Autobiography, Recruiting Campaign, 1918), yet he preached non-violence and no personal arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Lamented that military spending had grown after independence and wanted an army cut down and used only for policing (Harijan 7 December 1947; Young India 9 March 1922, India of My Dreams ch. 64); his police would be few and non-violent (Harijan 1 September 1940), and in Harijan (9 June 1946) he said democracy should cease to rely on the army for anything.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Said the state does not license houses of ill fame or cater to vices (Young India 8 June 1921) and looked to the day humanity would end prostitution (Young India 28 May 1925, India of My Dreams ch. 54).

decide-locally.rationale: His 1946 vision places full powers in village republics rather than a centralised pyramid.

rehabilitation.rationale: Said jails in free India should be hospitals where criminals are treated as patients (Harijan 5 May 1946; Delhi Diary, India of My Dreams ch. 64) and admitted he would only confine thieves as an imperfect fall from non-violence (Young India, My Non-violence).

traditional-family.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

abortion-legal.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

more-religion-public.rationale: He says his political activity is guided by religious moral responsibility beyond sectarian faith.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He makes ending untouchability a central obligation of the independence movement.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said Indian civilization is not to be beaten by any other and that India must keep its own culture while assimilating what is good from the West (Hind Swaraj, ch. XIII; Young India 11 August 1927).

gradual-change.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He welcomes a voluntary world federation of free nations and international arbitration of disputes.

free-trade.rationale: Said England sinned against India by forcing free trade on her, and that it was poison for this country (Speeches and Writings, 'The Gospel of Swadeshi', India of My Dreams ch. 31); the Karachi programme called for excluding foreign cloth and yarn.

nation-first.rationale: Said patriotism is humanity and his service of India must never harm other nations (Young India 16 March 1921; Harijan 17 November 1933, India of My Dreams ch. 3).

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He rejects defeating Hitlerism through superior violence and insists on nonviolent resistance.

open-borders.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

limit-growth.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He rejects the idea that machinery and material comforts constitute human improvement.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Said violent means give violent swaraj (Young India 17 July 1924) and that a bloody revolution is a certainty one day unless the rich voluntarily share (Constructive Programme, 'Economic Equality'); he sought change without violence.

experts-over-public.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: opposed concentrating economic control at the centre and said true democracy cannot be run by twenty men at the centre (Harijan 18 January 1948), while accepting nationalisation of heavy industry.

socialized-markets.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

land-value-tax.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Wrote in Harijan (31 July 1937) that inherited fortunes properly belong to the nation and that death duties should be imposed, since heirs of millionaires are harmed by the inheritance; Karachi resolution item on a graduated inheritance tax (1931).

basic-income.rationale: Opposed unconditional free food for the able-bodied on the ground that it breeds idleness and fraud (Young India 13 August 1925; Harijan 11 May 1935, India of My Dreams ch. 14).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Karachi resolution item 15 asked for protection of indigenous cloth by excluding foreign cloth and yarn, and in the Swadeshi chapter he approved of the sugar protection Natal gave itself; his aim was protecting hand industries rather than mills.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Said what India needs is distribution of capital within easy reach of the seven lakh villages, not concentration in a few hands (Young India 23 March 1921, India of My Dreams ch. 18); he also favoured collective village ownership of cattle and farms.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

one-party-rule.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Condemned the divine right of kings, saw princes as servants of the people who may be resisted if they fail (Harijan 6 July 1947) and in Hind Swaraj (ch. XV) opposed the tyranny of Indian princes as much as British rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Called disciplined, enlightened democracy the finest thing in the world but said an ignorant, prejudiced democracy lands in chaos (Young India 30 July 1931); he preferred reducing abuse to rejecting democracy (Young India 7 May 1931).

direct-votes.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

workers-councils.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Mixed: he fought partition, but said in Harijan (18 April 1942) that if the vast majority of Muslims regard themselves as a separate nation no power on earth can compel them to think otherwise, and in 1947 he held that accession of a princely state needs its people's consent (Delhi Diary, 11 November 1947).

natural-rulers.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

political-violence-never.rationale: His late writings insist nonviolence is the means to peace and reject retaliatory violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Called the Zulu campaign a man-hunt and said it showed him the horror of war (Autobiography, 'Heart Searchings'); in Hind Swaraj (ch. XVII) he said history as a record of wars would have ended the world.

separate-church-state.rationale: His 1946 statement explicitly separates personal religion from state affairs.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He refuses to turn a Hindu religious obligation into binding law for all Indians.

private-courts-defense.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

military-superiority.rationale: He condemns preparation for superior military violence as a threat to world peace.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wrote that India is one nation though peopled by Hindus, Muslims, Parsis and Christians and that foreigners merge in it; no part of the world has nationality and religion as synonyms (Hind Swaraj, ch. X).

class-struggle-history.rationale: Said class war is foreign to India's genius and avoidable (Amrita Bazar Patrika 3 August 1934), and in Hind Swaraj (ch. XVII) that history as usually told records interruptions of the force of love while the love-force itself works unrecorded.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He demands levelling down concentrated wealth and raising the impoverished millions.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: In Hind Swaraj (ch. XX) he told the English they may keep the riches already drained from India but must stop draining more; he demanded no reparations then or later.

civilizational-union.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Taught service and the reduction of wants as the basis of civilization and condemned mammon worship (Hind Swaraj, ch. XIII; Young India 24 June 1926, India of My Dreams ch. 13).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Taught that rights flow only from duties performed, and that people need to know their duties more than their rights (Harijan 25 March 1939, India of My Dreams chs. 2 and 11).

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Wanted identity with all life, even crawling creatures (Young India 4 April 1929), and found tree worship a beautiful reverence for the vegetable kingdom (Young India 26 September 1929).

limit-population.rationale: Mixed: urged regulating births by self-restraint and said rabbit-like breeding must stop (Harijan 31 March 1946), but denied India is over-populated and rejected artificial birth control (Young India 2 April 1925; Harijan 14 September 1935).

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He attacks industrial modern civilisation as morally destructive and enslaving.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Said it is criminal to displace hand labour with power-driven machinery unless the millions find other work (Young India 5 November 1925) and welcomed only simple tools that lighten the burden.

human-enhancement.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Wrote that to restore India to its pristine condition we must return to our own civilization, while allowing progress and reforms within it (Hind Swaraj, ch. XVIII).

results-over-ideology.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

direct-action.rationale: He advocates passive resistance and refusal to obey unjust laws rather than dependence on parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: He argues that means and ends are inseparable, comparing them to seed and tree.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Defined equal distribution as each person having what supplies his natural needs and no more, with a weak digestion needing less flour than a strong one (Harijan 25 August 1940, India of My Dreams ch. 18).

production-for-use.rationale: Wanted villages to be self-contained and to manufacture mainly for use rather than for sale (Harijan 29 August 1936, India of My Dreams chs. 7 and 26); khadi was meant to meet local needs first.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Denied that capitalists and landlords are exploiters by inherent necessity (Amrita Bazar Patrika 3 August 1934) while holding that exploitation depends on the exploited cooperating with it; he did accuse mills of exploiting villagers (India of My Dreams ch. 30).

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Said Russian-type communism imposed on a people would be repugnant to India and that Bolshevism's use of force for expropriation could not last (Young India 15 November 1928; Harijan 13 March 1937); he wanted any state to carry out the people's will, not dictate to them.

collective-farming.rationale: Wrote in Harijan (15 February 1942, India of My Dreams ch. 33) that it is far better for a hundred village families to cultivate their land collectively and share the produce, and that full benefit of agriculture will not come without cooperative farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred: described Western industrial civilization as having insatiable material ambition at one end and war at the other, and said mass production ties nations to exploiting weaker races (Harijan 2 November 1934, India of My Dreams ch. 7); he did not call it inevitable.

taxation-theft.rationale: In Harijan (8 September 1946, 'Taxes', India of My Dreams ch. 64) he said taxes should stand for the general benefit of society and that a popular ministry needs the voters' consent for them; he treated taxation as legitimate and urged citizens not to resent it.

harm-principle.rationale: Held that the state should prohibit drink even though drinkers mainly harm themselves and their families, since diseased persons must be helped against themselves (Young India 12 January 1928); this goes beyond preventing harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

conscription.rationale: Said he would oppose compulsory military training in every case, even under a national government (Young India 24 September 1925, My Non-violence).

exit-over-voice.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

state-as-business.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Karachi resolution he moved said political freedom must include real economic freedom of the starving millions, and he said the poor must have the ordinary amenities of life before swaraj is complete (Young India 26 March 1931).

media-academia-power.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

hereditarian-race.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

organic-representation.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

total-state.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

national-rebirth.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said he wanted India to rise without ruining other nations and that imperialism has no place in his scheme (Young India 12 March 1925; Young India 16 March 1921, India of My Dreams ch. 3).

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

bound-labor.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

universal-morality.rationale: Said fundamental ethics is common to all religions and that the state should teach it (Harijan 23 March 1947), though he based moral truth on truth-force and inner conviction more than reason.

single-common-good.rationale: Rejected the utilitarian greatest good of the greatest number for the greatest good of all (Young India 9 December 1926, India of My Dreams ch. 15), the sarvodaya ideal he took from Ruskin (Autobiography, 'The Magic Spell of a Book').

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Wrote that the cry for a national home for the Jews makes no appeal to him, that Palestine belongs to the Arabs as England belongs to the English, and that it is wrong to impose Jews on the Arabs (Harijan 26 November 1938).

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

revive-national-language.rationale: Praised efforts to revive Welsh and wanted India's languages revived against English (Hind Swaraj, ch. XVIII); the Autobiography (Recruiting Campaign) records his shame at the Viceroy's hall treating Hindustani speech as remarkable.

workplace-democracy.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

school-vouchers.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Said swaraj is a 'square' of political, economic, moral and religious independence that is out of shape if any side fails (Harijan 2 January 1937); his economic freedom means freedom for the masses, not market liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Wanted rulers to set a moral example, e.g. a governor who is teetotal, spins and lives in a cottage (Harijan 24 August 1947, India of My Dreams ch. 67), and held that legislation alone cannot reform society (Young India 30 June 1927).

national-self-determination.rationale: Said he wanted India's freedom without exploiting any other race and that every other race, weak or strong, has the same right to freedom (Young India 1 October 1931, India of My Dreams ch. 73).

force-without-un.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Repeatedly acted on an inner voice and prayer, e.g. the sudden decision to fast in the Ahmedabad strike (Autobiography, 'The Fast'), and said satyagraha needs a living faith in God (India of My Dreams ch. 25).

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Wrote that a healthy person should not get a free meal without honest work, with the rule 'no labour, no meal', and would end free-meal houses if he could (Young India 13 August 1925, 'Beggary', India of My Dreams ch. 14); the disabled he said should be supported by the state.

class-collaboration.rationale: His economic programme seeks to end conflict between capital and labour through trusteeship.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

dominated-front.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

workers-nation.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Believed women's sphere is mainly the home and men's the outside world (Speeches and Writings, India of My Dreams ch. 55) but insisted women suffer no legal disability and have the same civil rights (Young India 17 October 1929).

ban-interest.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In South Africa he contested the Natal Law Society's attempt to bar a coloured man from the bar (Autobiography, 'Colour Bar') and objected to the compulsory 'coolie locations', likening them to ghettoes (Autobiography, 'Coolie Locations or Ghettos?').

state-class-instrument.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said foreigners are welcome only if they regard themselves as one with the people (Harijan 29 September 1946) and urged refugees to blend with local people like sugar in milk (Delhi Diary p. 82); this concerns merging, not abandoning one's culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

proportional-representation.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

national-mission.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wrote that woman has been suppressed under custom and law shaped by men, that men consider themselves lords and masters, and that her legal and customary status demands radical change (Constructive Programme, 'Women').

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Called a law imposing sterilization on the people inhuman, though he thought voluntary sterilization desirable for individuals with chronic disease (Amrita Bazar Patrika 12 January 1935, India of My Dreams ch. 56).

security-forces-accountable.rationale: On the Amritsar massacre he did not press for General Dyer's punishment, only for stopping his pension (Young India, My Non-violence); the Congress did hold an inquiry into the Punjab atrocities (Autobiography, 'In the Punjab').

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wanted government to govern little, yet backed state control of key industries, prohibition, schooling and welfare of the poor (Karachi resolution 1931; Constructive Programme), so he did not confine it to defence and justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said all human beings are absolutely equal in soul and that assuming superiority over another is a sin against God and man (Young India 4 June 1931, India of My Dreams ch. 60); Ruskin's lesson that the lawyer and barber have equal right to a livelihood changed his life (Autobiography, 'The Magic Spell of a Book').

socialism-one-country.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Contested: said he would personally stop all conversions and propaganda except by conduct if he could (speech at Tirupur 19 March 1925; Harijan 1935 reported), yet held that any adult may change faith and that under swaraj all would be free to exercise their faiths.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: In July 1947 he explicitly rejects imposing a cow-slaughter ban on non-Hindus.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Said in Harijan (23 March 1947) that he did not think the state can concern itself with religious education, which belongs to religious associations, while fundamental ethics is for the state to teach; his earlier 1927 view favoured religious instruction in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Defined swaraj as government by the consent of the people as ascertained from the adult population (Young India 29 January 1925), and said true swaraj means citizens' capacity to resist authority when abused.

trade-surplus.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

population-transfer.rationale: He opposes expelling religious minorities and urges their safety in their existing homes.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Held that no reform is achieved by compulsion and that all force corrupts the end (Young India 8 December 1927, India of My Dreams ch. 64), though he accepted state restraint of thieves and drunkards as a lesser evil.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Praised ancient India for having no system of life-corroding competition (Hind Swaraj, ch. XIII) and wanted competition replaced by mutual service (India of My Dreams ch. 14).

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

separated-powers.rationale: Mixed: his village panchayat was to combine legislature, judiciary and executive for its one-year term (Harijan 26 July 1942), but he also wanted an incorruptible independent judiciary (Young India 27 August 1931) and governors able to check ministers (Harijan 21 December 1947).

vanguard-party.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Said swaraj must be the poor man's swaraj (Young India 26 March 1931) and that a national government must give preference to the downtrodden even if privileged classes object (The Nation's Voice, India of My Dreams ch. 64).

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Said it is absurd to say India is over-populated and that poverty comes from the extinction of village industries and the pressure on the land (Young India 3 November 1921; Harijan 11 May 1935, India of My Dreams ch. 12).

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said India's strength is its capacity to assimilate peoples of many faiths into one nation, and that Hindu-Muslim enmity is not inborn (Hind Swaraj, ch. X).

offices-by-lottery.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

party-controls-media.rationale: Wrote that freedom of the press is a precious privilege no country can forgo and that repressive ordinances do not work; he wanted any control to come from within journalism (Young India 28 May 1931, India of My Dreams ch. 68).

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Held that individual freedom can have full play only under non-violence and that suppressing opponents cannot produce true swaraj (Harijan 27 May 1939, India of My Dreams ch. 2); he put moral discipline before economic growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Wrote in Harijan (7 July 1946, 'Atom Bomb and Ahimsa') that the bomb brought an empty victory and cannot be undone by counter-bombs, as violence cannot be by counter-violence; mankind must get out of violence through non-violence.

central-bank-independence.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Wrote that there is no such thing as the divine right of kings to rule and the humble duty of subjects to obey (Harijan 6 July 1947, India of My Dreams ch. 11).

character-from-environment.rationale: Mixed: wrote that children inherit the qualities of their parents as well as physical traits, while environment also matters and purity can overcome evil inheritance (Autobiography, quoted in India of My Dreams ch. 58).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Held that rulers must act as servants and not rule by the right of the sword (Harijan 6 July 1947), and that ministers and legislators must be above suspicion and make no private gains (Harijan 23 April 1938).

space-expansion.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

leader-cult.rationale: Said in the last chapter of the Autobiography ('Farewell') that the world's praise fails to move him and often stings, and that he must reduce himself to zero.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

land-redistribution.rationale: Contested: said the land should belong to the tiller and not to absentee landlords, and that no one should hold more than he needs, but insisted on non-violent means and no forcible ejection (Harijan 20 April 1940); he allowed state confiscation with minimum violence if trusteeship failed (Modern Review 1933).

refugee-return.rationale: Said Muslims who had not freely chosen to migrate to Pakistan should be asked by their neighbours to return to their homes with a feeling of safety (Delhi Diary p. 19, India of My Dreams ch. 71); he did not speak of descendants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Said it is open to any person of mature age to change faith when and as often as he wishes (speech at Tirupur, 19 March 1925, in 'Gandhiji on Religious Conversion').

women-must-cover.rationale: Condemned the purdah as barbarous and useless (Autobiography, 'Playing the Husband') and said chastity cannot be protected by a wall, since it grows from within (Young India 3 February 1927, India of My Dreams ch. 54).

common-currency.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Told German Jews to claim Germany as their home and resist expulsion by non-violent civil resistance, and said persecuted Jews should be treated justly wherever born (Harijan 26 November 1938).

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

ban-cartels.rationale: Said he was personally opposed to great trusts and to concentration of industries by elaborate machinery (Young India 24 July 1924, India of My Dreams ch. 30) and that machinery used to concentrate wealth is wrong.

no-bailouts.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Said the rule of the majority becomes intolerable when coercive and that a minority has a right to act differently (Young India 26 January 1922 and 2 March 1932, India of My Dreams ch. 4), a point he wanted guarded by constitutional rights (Karachi resolution 1931).

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Rejected an economy that lives off others: India must be neither exploiter nor exploited, and a British Lancashire should stand aside for Indian cottages (India of My Dreams chs. 1 and 31); his self-sufficiency was village-level and was not a closed imperial bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Held that intellectual work should never demand payment and that in the ideal state doctors and lawyers work purely for society (India of My Dreams ch. 14), and that trustees should earn for service rather than for self (Harijan 22 February 1942).

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Stated that hereditary inequalities must go as injurious to society (Harijan 6 July 1947) and called for non-cooperation with government titles and honours (Autobiography, 'The Khilafat against Cow Protection?').

history-own-civilization.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Wrote that the English hold India only because Indians keep them there and that foreign rule must go (Hind Swaraj, chs. VII and XIV); early in life he held the Empire a power for good (Autobiography, 'Passion for Unity'), but he rejected it from 1920.

elective-rulers.rationale: Said hereditary inequalities must go and there is no divine right of kings, rulers rule by right of service, and princes who fail may be resisted (Harijan 6 July 1947, India of My Dreams ch. 11).

minority-veto.rationale: Said it is a superstition that a majority's act binds a minority (Hind Swaraj, ch. XVII) and that the minority has a perfect right to act differently from the majority, which is to be followed only in matters of detail (Young India 2 March 1932).

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Said that if a prince fails to act as servant of the people, the ryots have a duty to resist the usurpation, but without murder or plunder (Harijan 6 July 1947, India of My Dreams ch. 11).

parliament-supreme.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Contested: opposed killing animals for medical research (Hind Swaraj, ch. XII) and personally avoided meat, but promoted humane keeping of cattle for milk and draught and reluctantly took goat's milk (Autobiography, 'The Rowlatt Bills and My Dilemma').

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Called on the rich, zamindars and princes to act as trustees for the poor, reduce their own wants and surrender superfluities (Young India 5 December 1929, India of My Dreams ch. 22; Constructive Programme, 'Economic Equality').

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Wrote in the closing chapter of the Autobiography ('Farewell') that his devotion to Truth drew him into politics and that those who say religion has nothing to do with politics do not know what religion means; a seeker cannot keep out of any field of life.

office-by-exam.rationale: Said the lowest government posts should be filled by examination by an impartial board and that the fittest should hold office regardless of community (Young India 29 May 1924, India of My Dreams ch. 66).

single-official-language.rationale: Wanted Hindustani as the common language of India but provincial languages as the media of schooling and public work, and reorganised provinces on language lines (Constructive Programme, 'Provincial Languages' and 'National Language'; India of My Dreams ch. 65).

democratic-peace.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Held that a satyagrahi must first render willing and intelligent obedience to the laws of society and may disobey only unjust ones, and only with readiness to take the penalty (Autobiography, 'A Himalayan Miscalculation'; Young India 3 November 1921).

treaties-binding.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: His village republic was to be run on a cooperative basis, with a panchayat of five elected annually, compulsory service by village guards and no caste distinctions (Harijan 26 July 1942, India of My Dreams ch. 24).

majority-settlement.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Said every school of honest thought must have room and that intolerance betrays want of faith in one's cause (Young India 17 April 1924 and 2 February 1921, India of My Dreams chs. 4 and 75).

punish-blasphemy.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Told the English to stop draining India's wealth and to stop commercial exploitation (Hind Swaraj, ch. XX) and urged that the connection be a voluntary partnership (Young India 24 December 1931).

assisted-dying.rationale: After having a suffering ashram calf put down by injection in 1928 (Navajivan), he said he would apply the same principle to human beings and to himself, like a surgeon's knife used in the sufferer's interest; known to us only through this quotation.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

alienated-labor.rationale: Said factory workers are worse off than beasts, enslaved by money and made cowardly by machine work (Hind Swaraj, ch. VI and XIX), and blamed the divorce of intellect from bodily labour for rural decline (Constructive Programme, 'Village Sanitation').

islam-incompatible.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Said power resides in the people and is entrusted to chosen representatives (Constructive Programme, 'Communal Unity'), and defined swaraj as rule by the people's consent (Young India 29 January 1925).

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

social-market-economy.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Said in Harijan (1 September 1940) that he had the courage to say a non-violent state can do without an army, though not without police, and hoped India would show the way (India of My Dreams ch. 20); in 1947 he conceded he could not impose this on the Union Cabinet (My Non-violence, Kashmir).

rich-first.rationale: Gave as a golden rule to refuse to have what millions cannot, and said that a few may not live in jewelled palaces while millions live in hovels (Young India 24 June 1926; Harijan 25 March 1939, India of My Dreams chs. 2 and 13).

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

property-franchise.rationale: Said he was wedded to adult suffrage and could not bear that a man of character but no wealth or literacy should have no vote (Young India 8 October 1931, India of My Dreams ch. 64).

domination-women-nature.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

reification.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He calls nonviolent government impossible while a vast gulf separates rich and hungry people.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Said India will never be godless and that rank atheism cannot flourish here (Hind Swaraj, ch. XVIII), and wanted no state promotion of denominational religion either (Harijan 23 March 1947).

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Said a police force may be necessary even in a non-violent state, a sign of his imperfect ahimsa (Harijan 1 September 1940), and wanted jails turned into hospitals rather than abolished.

culture-before-state.rationale: Said swaraj is worth nothing unless it purifies civilization (Young India 23 January 1930) and urged constructive moral and economic work rather than a scramble for power (Constructive Programme; India of My Dreams ch. 70).

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 172 answers taken from it, 26 agreed, 2 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Researched from the maintainer-supplied Autobiography (1927-29, covering his life to 1921; read chapter by chapter for the personal and campaign record), Hind Swaraj (1909), and, for his 1921-1948 positions, the dated Young India, Harijan and speech extracts in India of My Dreams and My Non-violence, the Constructive Programme (1945), the Karachi resolution and his 1938 statement on Palestine. Later positions override the Autobiography and Hind Swaraj: he supported the British in the Boer War (1899), the Zulu campaign (1906) and WWI recruiting (1918) as a loyal subject and rejected the Empire from 1920, and in Hind Swaraj he called railways, lawyers and doctors harmful but later accepted simple tools and limited key-industry nationalisation. He defended varna (hereditary occupational divisions) while condemning untouchability and caste hierarchy, and early South African writing on Africans is criticised by scholars (see Wikipedia). Answers resting on secondary quotation only (assisted dying, right to secede) are medium or low. Statements on topics he never addressed (abortion, same-sex questions, healthcare policy, most monetary and technology policy) are null.
